title:
ICE Agents and Deputies Pull Suspected Illegal Alien Alberto Lira Razo Out of His Van in Hamilton, Ohio

On November 6 i
title_en:
ICE Agents and Deputies Pull Suspected Illegal Alien Alberto Lira Razo Out of His Van in Hamilton, Ohio

On November 6 in Hamilton, Ohio, Alberto Lira Razo went live on Facebook from inside his car as officers surrounded it.  An agent at his window is wearing a vest marked ICE with a DHS patch.

Razo told the deputy to "Break it. Break it." and the deputy did exactly that.

His daughter, Loudmouth Lupe, filmed from outside.  Officers in POLICE and SHERIFF vests pull him out of a white van with a smashed window.

Then they shove and body-block her while she's filming.  She can be heard saying, "Get off of me, I am a child!"

On the tape, she says they tased and punched her dad.  Neither is shown in either video.

He's reportedly 38 and was booked on an ICE hold.  No agency has released a statement, and no charges have been announced.

Hamilton is the seat of Butler County, where Sheriff Richard Jones runs a 287(g) agreement with ICE.  That lets trained deputies use limited immigration authority during routine stops.

Jones has said ICE trained 44 of his deputies.  Immigration arrests in Hamilton more than quadrupled through July compared to the same stretch last year.

full_text_zh:
ICE 特工和副手在俄亥俄州汉密尔顿将疑似非法外国人阿尔贝托·里拉·拉佐 (Alberto Lira Razo) 从他的货车中拉出来

11 月 6 日，在俄亥俄州汉密尔顿，阿尔贝托·里拉·拉佐 (Alberto Lira Razo) 在车内通过 Facebook 进行直播，当时警察包围了车子。 一名特工站在窗口，穿着一件带有 ICE 标记和 DHS 补丁的背心。

拉佐告诉副警长“打破它。打破它。”副手正是这样做的。

他的女儿劳德茅斯·卢佩 (Loudmouth Lupe) 在外面拍摄。 身着警察和警长背心的警察将他从一辆窗户被砸碎的白色货车中拉出来。

然后他们在她拍摄时推搡并用身体挡住她。 可以听到她说：“放开我，我还是个孩子！”

在录音中，她说他们殴打了她的父亲。 两个视频中都没有显示。

据报道，他今年 38 岁，并被 ICE 拘留。 没有机构发表声明，也没有宣布任何指控。

汉密尔顿是巴特勒县的县治，治安官理查德·琼斯 (Richard Jones) 与 ICE 签订了 287(g) 协议。 这使得训练有素的警员在例行停留期间可以使用有限的移民权力。

琼斯表示，ICE 培训了 44 名副手。 与去年同期相比，7 月份汉密尔顿逮捕的移民人数增加了四倍多。

🚨 Fable 5.5 TESTING Part 14

⚡ I asked Claude to ride a lightning bolt from cloud to ground.

One prompt. I never touched the code. 🤯

⏱️ 182 minutes
💸 $17.57 in API costs
🤖 Claude Fable 5.5 Xhigh in Claude Code

⛈️ Simulated the storm on a 30.5M-cell grid: rising air, rain, ice and electric charge, with 63 flashes logged

🚨 Scanned every frame, found a full-screen strobe at 4 to 6 Hz and fixed it before I ever saw it

📦 28 s · one unbroken shot · 1080p60 · three.js + Taichi

title: Imagine giving one AI agent a video idea and getting back a finished production without having to manage five different
title_en:
Imagine giving one AI agent a video idea and getting back a finished production without having to manage five different tools.
That's what @termix_ai is demonstrating with its new Montage Studio Agent.

Instead of trying to handle every part of production itself, Montage Studio hires other specialized agents to do the work.

Here's how it works:
- submit your brief for a music video or ad.
- Montage Studio creates the treatment and beat timed shot list.
- it hires agents to create storyboard frames, compose music and render video shots.
- the different pieces are brought together and edited.
- you receive a finished 1080p video.

The interesting part is how the work gets coordinated.
Each hired agent has its own task, quote and payment settled through TermiX escrow.
One agent manages the project while other agents provide the specialized services.

This is a practical example of what an agent economy could look like.
Agents don't necessarily need to do everything themselves, they can focus on what they're good at and hire other agents for the rest.

There's also a live campaign around Montage Studio.
Complete your first order of at least 31.5 USDC and earn 15,750 TermiX Points.

- You need to bind your X account, and the order must be completed and settled onchain. the reward is limited to one qualifying order per wallet.

This is more interesting than another AI agent demo.
We're seeing agents coordinate paid work, hire other agents and deliver an actual product.

title:
AI has made it incredibly easy to build an app, but choosing the right architecture is still a different skill.

Postgre
title_en:
AI has made it incredibly easy to build an app, but choosing the right architecture is still a different skill.

Postgres is a great default, but it isn't the answer to every problem. Some applications need the speed of Redis, others need document databases, and some need a completely different approach.

The problem with vibe coding is that developers can generate working software without understanding why certain technologies were chosen in the first place.

Being able to build an app with Claude is impressive. Knowing which tools to use, when to use them, and why is what separates builders from people simply generating code.
title_zh:
人工智能使构建应用程序变得异常容易，但选择正确的架构仍然是一项不同的技能。

Postgres 是一个很好的默认设置，但它并不能解决所有问题。有些应用程序需要 Redis 的速度，有些应用程序需要文档数据库，有些则需要完全不同的方法。

title: In May and June, I exposed how Iranian operative and alleged Iranian regime lobbyist Trita Parsi  was in communication w
title_en:
In May and June, I exposed how Iranian operative and alleged Iranian regime lobbyist Trita Parsi  was in communication with White House officials who were leaking to him about the Iran war. @tparsi 

Now, months later, it appears someone is leaking situation room meetings to Trita Parsi. 

You’ll recall I reported earlier this year that Trita Parsi was allegedly marked for deportation by the Trump administration after he was flagged as a risk by Secretary of State Marco Rubio @SecRubio. This was even confirmed to me in May by a State Department official. 

Source: https://t.co/UNiiHY091B

The Quincy Institute then circulated an internal memo about how they were going to cover Tita’s defense with immigration lawyers, and the memo, which cited me, was leaked to me, confirming that Trita was facing the possibility of deportation. 

Source: https://t.co/RgsNkb5WjL

Trita is not a US citizen. He has Iranian and Swedish citizenship. Multiple GOP Senators have called for Trita to be investigated as an alleged lobbyist for the Iranian regime. In 2020, Senators @tedcruz, @SenTomCotton, and then Senator @GovBraun Mike Braun, who is the current Governor of Indiana, called on the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) to investigate the National Iranian American Council (NIAC), a lobby group they believe acts as a "foreign agent of the Islamic Republic.”

Trita likely was going to be deported, until he and his colleagues at Quincy allegedly called in a favor to a very senior  official at the White House. 

Any wild guesses who that is? 🤔 

Now, Trita has not been deported, and he is suggesting that highly private information from the Situation Room is being leaked to him. 

@SecRubio this would be the perfect time before the Democrats take over in January for you to revoke Trita Parsi’s visa and have him removed from our country. 

Again, I flagged all of this for the WH over 6 months ago.

It won’t end well. 

Deport Trita Parsi!

full_text_zh:
5 月和 6 月，我揭露了伊朗特工和所谓的伊朗政权游说者特里塔·帕西 (Trita Parsi) 如何与向他泄露伊朗战争信息的白宫官员进行沟通。 @tparsi

现在，几个月后，似乎有人正在向特里塔·帕西泄露战情室会议内容。

你可能还记得我今年早些时候报道过，特里塔·帕西 (Trita Parsi) 据称被国务卿马可·卢比奥 (Marco Rubio) @SecRubio 标记为风险后，被特朗普政府标记为驱逐出境。一位国务院官员甚至在五月份向我证实了这一点。

资料来源：

昆西研究所随后散发了一份内部备忘录，说明他们将如何与移民律师一起为蒂塔辩护，这份引用了我的备忘录被泄露给了我，确认蒂塔面临着被驱逐出境的可能性。

资料来源：

Trita 不是美国公民。他拥有伊朗和瑞典国籍。多位共和党参议员呼吁对特里塔作为伊朗政权的游说者进行调查。 2020 年，参议员 @tedcruz、@SenTomCotton 以及现任参议员 @GovBraun、现任印第安纳州州长迈克·布劳恩 (Mike Braun) 呼吁美国司法部 (DoJ) 调查伊朗裔美国人全国委员会 (NIAC)，他们认为该游说团体是“伊斯兰共和国的外国代理人”。

特里塔很可能会被驱逐出境，直到据称他和他在昆西的同事向白宫一位非常高级的官员求助。

大家猜猜那是谁吗？ 🤔

现在，特里塔还没有被驱逐出境，他暗示战情室的高度私密信息正在泄露给他。

@SecRubio，这将是民主党一月份上台之前撤销 Trita Parsi 签证并将他驱逐出我国的最佳时机。

6 个多月前，我再次向白宫提出了所有这些问题。

结局不会好。

驱逐特里塔·帕西！

title:
Don’t just trust an AI’s answer verify how it was generated.

An AI agent might arrive at the correct result while skipp
title_en:
Don’t just trust an AI’s answer verify how it was generated.

An AI agent might arrive at the correct result while skipping half the steps you expected it to take. For a simple query, that might not matter. @primus_labs 

But when an agent handles money, data, or critical decisions, a "correct result" isn't enough; you also need to know how it got there.

This is the trust issue that Primus Labs aims to address through verifiable agent execution. 

The approach uses zkTLS proofs to demonstrate that the necessary API calls actually took place. 

These proofs capture key details of the requests and responses without exposing private credentials or the entirety of the session data.

Consider a trading agent: before placing an order, it must check the price from a trusted oracle. 

Typically, you would simply have to take the agent’s word that it did so. With zkTLS, the agent can provide proof that the call to the oracle actually occurred. 

A verifier can then confirm that the critical steps took place in the expected sequence checking the oracle first, followed by placing the order.

What’s significant here is a shift in perspective: instead of trusting an agent’s output, we verify the process that produced it. 

Trust is no longer based on reputation or promises, but on verifiable evidence.

This leaves a question for you: if every critical step taken by an AI agent could be proven, would you be more inclined to trust it? @primus_labs 

For me, the answer is almost certainly yes as AI agents are granted increasing levels of autonomy, verifiability will become the cornerstone of trust.

full_text_zh:
不要只相信人工智能的答案，验证它是如何生成的。

人工智能代理可能会跳过您预期要执行的一半步骤，从而得出正确的结果。对于简单的查询，这可能并不重要。 @primus_labs

但是，当代理处理资金、数据或关键决策时，“正确的结果”是不够的；还需要有“正确的结果”。你还需要知道它是如何到达那里的。

这是 Primus Labs 旨在通过可验证的代理执行来解决的信任问题。

该方法使用 zkTLS 证明来证明必要的 API 调用确实发生了。

这些证明捕获请求和响应的关键细节，而不会暴露私人凭证或整个会话数据。

考虑一个交易代理：在下订单之前，它必须检查来自可信预言机的价格。

通常情况下，您只需相信代理人的话即可。通过 zkTLS，代理可以提供对预言机的调用实际发生的证据。

然后，验证者可以首先检查预言机，然后下订单，以确认关键步骤按照预期顺序发生。

这里重要的是视角的转变：我们不再信任代理的输出，而是验证产生它的过程。

信任不再基于声誉或承诺，而是基于可验证的证据。

这给你留下了一个问题：如果人工智能代理采取的每一个关键步骤都可以被证明，你会更倾向于信任它吗？ @primus_labs

对我来说，答案几乎肯定是肯定的，随着人工智能代理被授予越来越多的自主权，可验证性将成为信任的基石。

title_en:
Claude Code really spent $102 and 28 minutes building a lighthouse while Blender MCP made a cinematic ocean disaster for $67 😭

Meanwhile GPT-6 Astra charged $40 to build a lighthouse that looks like a toilet paper roll sitting in a blue puddle 💀

Same prompt, 4 AI workflows

The damage report 🌊

🥇 Blender MCP → $67 / 20 min

Kimi was 8.5x cheaper and 9.3x faster than Claude Code

Blender MCP actually delivered the most cinematic result with massive waves, dramatic lighting and a lighthouse that looks straight out of a movie

Meanwhile Kimi went full Minecraft and GPT Astra apparently discovered low-poly oceans 😭

The cheapest AI won on price, but the best-looking scene is a completely different story

Imagine you own an AI agent specialized in market research.

Initially, it might only provid
title_en:
Good afternoon @termix_ai 

Imagine you own an AI agent specialized in market research.

Initially, it might only provide data analysis reports. But over time, clients start asking for more: data collection, competitor monitoring, trend analysis, and comprehensive reporting.

Should the agent expand its service offerings, or should it remain focused on a single area of ​​expertise?

In my view, this is a compelling business challenge within the "AI agent economy."

Specialization helps an agent establish a clear competitive edge, while expanding services opens doors to a wider range of client needs and revenue opportunities.

The next question is: how can clients truly understand what an agent is capable of doing?

On @termix_ai , https://t.co/qOt62czV2r provides an environment where agents can build service pages and list exactly what they offer.

A strong listing requires more than just an engaging service name. It must clearly define:
• What problem is the client trying to solve?
• What inputs does the agent need to perform the task?
• What are the specific deliverables?
• What are the costs and the scope of the service?

An agent with extensive capabilities may fail to attract clients if it cannot effectively communicate its value.

Conversely, a highly specialized service with clearly defined outputs can build trust and create a distinct competitive advantage.

I believe the future of AI agent marketplaces depends not just on the sheer number of agents, but on the ability to translate AI capabilities into tangible services that people actually want to hire.

full_text_en:
Good afternoon @termix_ai 

Imagine you own an AI agent specialized in market research.

Initially, it might only provide data analysis reports. But over time, clients start asking for more: data collection, competitor monitoring, trend analysis, and comprehensive reporting.

Should the agent expand its service offerings, or should it remain focused on a single area of ​​expertise?

In my view, this is a compelling business challenge within the "AI agent economy."

Specialization helps an agent establish a clear competitive edge, while expanding services opens doors to a wider range of client needs and revenue opportunities.

The next question is: how can clients truly understand what an agent is capable of doing?

On @termix_ai , https://t.co/qOt62czV2r provides an environment where agents can build service pages and list exactly what they offer.

A strong listing requires more than just an engaging service name. It must clearly define:
• What problem is the client trying to solve?
• What inputs does the agent need to perform the task?
• What are the specific deliverables?
• What are the costs and the scope of the service?

An agent with extensive capabilities may fail to attract clients if it cannot effectively communicate its value.

Conversely, a highly specialized service with clearly defined outputs can build trust and create a distinct competitive advantage.

I believe the future of AI agent marketplaces depends not just on the sheer number of agents, but on the ability to translate AI capabilities into tangible services that people actually want to hire.
full_text_zh:
下午好@termix_ai

想象一下，您拥有一个专门从事市场研究的人工智能代理。

最初，它可能只提供数据分析报告。但随着时间的推移，客户开始要求更多：数据收集、竞争对手监控、趋势分析和综合报告。

代理商应该扩大其服务范围，还是应该继续专注于单一专业领域？

在我看来，这是“人工智能代理经济”中一个引人注目的商业挑战。

专业化有助于代理商建立明显的竞争优势，同时扩展服务为更广泛的客户需求和收入机会打开了大门。

下一个问题是：客户如何才能真正了解代理人的能力？

在 @termix_ai 上， 提供了一个环境，代理可以在其中构建服务页面并准确列出他们提供的服务。

一个强大的列表需要的不仅仅是一个有吸引力的服务名称。它必须明确定义：
• 客户试图解决什么问题？
• 代理需要哪些输入来执行任务？
• 具体可交付成果是什么？
• 服务的费用和范围是多少？

拥有广泛能力的代理商如果不能有效地传达其价值，可能无法吸引客户。

相反，具有明确定义输出的高度专业化服务可以建立信任并创造独特的竞争优势。

我相信人工智能代理市场的未来不仅取决于代理的绝对数量，还取决于将人工智能功能转化为人们真正想要雇用的有形服务的能力。

title_en:
BREAKING: A 10-second video of a vibecoded dashboard losing its AI look just passed 1.9 million views, and you can now run that cleanup on your own pages in Claude Code, with a second agent flagging anything it changed beyond styling and copy.

I wrote a prompt that runs a designer's redline process on a real page in your repo, adapted from Damir Sokolovsky's open-source unslop skill (CC BY 4.0, link in the first reply) and rebuilt for pages that already have features and users.

Damir made that video too, it has almost as many bookmarks as likes on X, and the free skill he published three days later passed 5,500 GitHub stars in under four days, which tells you how many people are staring at the same purple gradient.

What it does:

→ Before screenshots at desktop and phone width through Chrome DevTools MCP, plus a build, test and Lighthouse accessibility baseline
→ A numbered slop list, a three-line direction and a table of proposed copy edits, and then it stops for your OK
→ Nine passes on a branch with one commit each: spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals, motion
→ A WCAG AA text contrast rule, checked once at the end with Lighthouse, which can't score text over images or gradients, so those get listed as unchecked
→ A fresh judge subagent, not a fork, handed only the screenshots and slop list, marks what's still there, and says can't tell for what stills can't show
→ A second fresh subagent that sees only the rules, the approved copy rows and the diff lists every change that isn't styling or approved copy

Two limits you should know about: the stop for your OK is an instruction rather than a lock, because Claude Code starts in auto mode, and if your page has no tests it clicks only the controls that can't write, send, delete or pay and tells you that's weaker proof instead of claiming nothing broke.

[ALEX: run it first and add one true line here]

Paste this into Claude Code:

<task>
Strip the AI look from [PAGE: local dev URL]. Change the craft only: features, behavior, facts and section order stay. No new sections or components.
</task>

<before>
Read-only until I approve. Use Chrome DevTools MCP. Leave any login to me and never read credentials.
- Save before shots outside the repo, emulating 1440x900 and 390x844, in screen-height pieces.
- Record the build and test results and lighthouse_audit accessibility failures on desktop and mobile.
</before>

<plan>
1. Slop list: number every sign of AI slop and where it shows: purple gradients, glows, gradient text, emoji labels, sparkle badges, wide-tracked caps, endless loops, drifting spacing. If the page is mostly fine, say so and fix only these.
2. Direction, three lines.
World: its setting or material.
Focus: 1-2 spots get rich color and detail, the rest stays quiet.
Signature: one small detail only this product would have.
Real brand colors, logos and fonts stay (a purple gradient isn't one).
3. Copy table, current vs proposed, tone only: exclamation marks, "Welcome back" greetings, hype words. No claim, number, price, name or legal line changes.
Show me all three, then stop and wait for my OK.
</plan>

<passes>
After my OK, on a new branch, one commit per pass across the whole page:
1. Spacing: 4px grid, same things same size
2. Color: one neutral scale tinted toward World, three text levels, one accent saved for Focus spots, no hue gradients or glows
3. Icons: the project's line icons replace emoji, one size and stroke
4. Copy: approved rows only
5. Type: weights 400 and 500, sentence case, the project's font
6. Layout: alignment and proportions inside sections only
7. Details: consistent radii, quiet badges, the Signature
8. Visuals: remove decorative filler, generate nothing
9. Motion: remove loops, transition-all, hover scale-ups
</passes>

<rules>
- Only styling and approved copy change. Anything else (logic, data, config, a new package or font) goes on an approval list, unbuilt.
- Theme files count as styling; name any other pages a change reaches.
- Keep every id, data- and aria- attribute. Never edit a test to pass it: copy-only breaks go on the approval list.
- Text stays at WCAG AA: 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text. Every control keeps a visible focus state.
- Never push or merge.
</rules>

<check>
After the last commit, retake the same shots, then:
- Build and tests: no new failures. No tests? Click only controls that can't write, send, delete or pay, and call that weaker proof.
- Rerun lighthouse_audit: no new failures. It can't score text over images or gradients, so list those as unchecked. Tab through to see focus states. Grep for motion items stills can't show.
- Judge, a fresh subagent, not a fork: gets only the before and after shots and slop list, edits nothing. Marks each item gone, still there or can't tell, citing the screenshot. Flags anything broken at phone width. Swap test: would this page still make sense with another company's name?
- Guard, same terms: gets only the rules above, approved copy rows and full branch diff. Lists every change that isn't styling or approved copy.
</check>

<stop>
Wait for both reports, fix what they find, then retake shots and rerun the check with a new judge and guard, 2 rounds max, then stop even if items remain. Failed swap test: push World and Signature, styling only. If frozen copy causes it, just report it.
</stop>

<output>
Final slop marks, test and Lighthouse results, approval list. End with what you need from me: merge, revert, or a call on each approval.
</output>

Adapted from unslop by Damir Sokolovsky, CC BY 4.0.

- Only styling and approved copy change. Anything else (logic, data, config, a new package or font) goes on an approval list, unbuilt.
- Theme files count as styling; name any other pages a change reaches.
- Keep every id, data- and aria- attribute. Never edit a test to pass it: copy-only breaks go on the approval list.
- Text stays at WCAG AA: 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text. Every control keeps a visible focus state.
- Never push or merge.
</rules>

<check>
After the last commit, retake the same shots, then:
- Build and tests: no new failures. No tests? Click only controls that can't write, send, delete or pay, and call that weaker proof.
- Rerun lighthouse_audit: no new failures. It can't score text over images or gradients, so list those as unchecked. Tab through to see focus states. Grep for motion items stills can't show.
- Judge, a fresh subagent, not a fork: gets only the before and after shots and slop list, edits nothing. Marks each item gone, still there or can't tell, citing the screenshot. Flags anything broken at phone width. Swap test: would this page still make sense with another company's name?
- Guard, same terms: gets only the rules above, approved copy rows and full branch diff. Lists every change that isn't styling or approved copy.
</check>

<stop>
Wait for both reports, fix what they find, then retake shots and rerun the check with a new judge and guard, 2 rounds max, then stop even if items remain. Failed swap test: push World and Signature, styling only. If frozen copy causes it, just report it.
</stop>

<output>
Final slop marks, test and Lighthouse results, approval list. End with what you need from me: merge, revert, or a call on each approval.
</output>

我编写了一个提示，在您的存储库中的真实页面上运行设计师的红线流程，改编自 Damir Sokolovsky 的开源 unslop 技能（CC BY 4.0，第一个回复中的链接），并为已经具有功能和用户的页面重新构建。

Damir 也制作了那个视频，它的书签数量几乎与 X 上的点赞数量一样多，三天后他发布的免费技能在四天内就超过了 5,500 个 GitHub star，这告诉你有多少人在盯着同一个紫色渐变。

它的作用：

→ 在通过 Chrome DevTools MCP 在桌面和手机宽度上进行屏幕截图之前，加上构建、测试和 Lighthouse 可访问性基线
→ 一个编号的倾斜列表、一个三行方向和一个建议的副本编辑表，然后它会停止以供您选择
→ 在一个分支上进行九次传递，每次提交一次：间距、颜色、图标、副本、类型、布局、细节、视觉效果、动作
→ WCAG AA 文本对比规则，最后用 Lighthouse 检查一次，它不能在图像或渐变上对文本进行评分，因此这些规则被列为未检查
→ 一位新的法官副代理人，而不是叉子，只递给屏幕截图和残渣清单，标记仍然存在的内容，并说无法分辨哪些剧照无法显示
→ 第二个新的子代理仅查看规则、批准的副本行和差异，列出了非样式或批准的副本的所有更改

您应该了解两个限制：“OK”的停止是一个指令而不是一个锁，因为 Claude Code 以自动模式启动，如果您的页面没有测试，它只会单击无法写入、发送、删除或支付的控件，并告诉您这是较弱的证据，而不是声称没有任何损坏。

[ALEX：先运行它并在此处添加一行]

将其粘贴到 Claude Code 中：

<任务>
从 [PAGE: local dev URL] 中剥离 AI 外观。仅更改工艺：特征、行为、事实和部分顺序保留。没有新的部分或组件。
</任务>

<之前>
在我批准之前只读。使用 Chrome 开发者工具 MCP。将任何登录信息留给我，并且永远不要阅读凭据。
- 在存储库之外保存之前的镜头，以屏幕高度的形式模拟 1440x900 和 390x844。
- 记录桌面和移动设备上的构建和测试结果以及 lighthouse_audit 可访问性失败。
</之前>

<计划>
1. 倾斜列表：对 AI 倾斜的每个标志及其显示位置进行编号：紫色渐变、发光、渐变文本、表情符号标签、闪光徽章、宽轨帽、无限循环、漂移间距。如果页面大部分都很好，请说出来并仅修复这些。
2.方向，三线。
世界：它的环境或材料。
焦点：1-2 个点获得丰富的色彩和细节，其余的保持安静。
签名：只有该产品才会有的一个小细节。
真正的品牌颜色、徽标和字体得以保留（紫色渐变不是其中之一）。
3. 复制表格，当前与建议，仅语气：感叹号、“欢迎回来”问候语、炒作词。索赔、数量、价格、名称或法律界限没有变化。
把三个都给我看，然后停下来等我同意。
</计划>

<通行证>
确定后，在一个新分支上，整个页面每次提交一次：
1.间距：4px网格，同物同尺寸
2. 颜色：一种向世界着色的中性比例，三个文本级别，一种为焦点保存的重音，无色调渐变或发光
3.图标：项目的线条图标替换了表情符号、一种尺寸和笔画
4. 复制：仅限批准的行
5. 类型：粗细400和500、句子大小写、项目的字体
6. 布局：仅部分内部的对齐和比例
7. 细节：一致的半径、安静的徽章、签名
8. 视觉效果：去除装饰性填充物，不产生任何东西
9. 运动：删除循环、全部过渡、悬停放大
</pass>

<规则>
- 仅样式和批准的副本更改。其他任何东西（逻辑、数据、配置、新包或字体）都在批准列表中，未构建。
- 主题文件算作样式；列出更改到达的任何其他页面。
- 保留每个 id、data- 和 aria- 属性。切勿编辑测试以通过它：仅复制的中断会出现在批准列表中。
- 文本保持 WCAG AA：4.5:1，或大文本为 3:1。每个控件都保持可见的焦点状态。
- 切勿推送或合并。
</规则>

<检查>
最后一次提交后，重新拍摄相同的镜头，然后：
- 构建和测试：没有新的失败。没有测试？仅单击无法写入、发送、删除或支付的控件，并调用该较弱的证明。
- 重新运行 lighthouse_audit：没有新的故障。它无法对图像或渐变上的文本进行评分，因此将它们列为未选中状态。按 T​​ab 浏览可查看焦点状态。 Grep 无法显示运动项目静止图像。
- 法官，一个新的副代理人，而不是叉子：只获取前后镜头和污点列表，不进行任何编辑。引用屏幕截图，将每个项目标记为消失、仍然存在或无法辨别。标记任何在手机宽度上损坏的东西。交换测试：此页面与其他公司的名称仍然有意义吗？
- Guard，相同条款：仅获取上述规则、批准的副本行和完整分支差异。列出所有非样式或批准副本的更改。
</检查>

<停止>
等待两份报告，修复他们发现的问题，然后重新拍摄并与新的法官和警卫重新进行检查，最多 2 轮，然后即使物品仍然存在也停止。交换测试失败：推送 World 和 Signature，仅样式。如果冻结副本导致此问题，只需报告即可。
</停止>

<输出>
最终斜坡标记、测试和灯塔结果、批准列表。以您需要我提供的内容结束：合并、恢复或对每个批准进行调用。
</输出>

改编自 Damir Sokolovsky 的 unslop，CC BY 4.0。

AI is either neutral for manufacturing, or massively positive for novel-drug manufact
title_en:
Biggest takeaway from CPHI Milan:

AI is either neutral for manufacturing, or massively positive for novel-drug manufacturing.

AI can design better molecules and get them into Phase 1 faster.

But it cannot manufacture them.

Thermo Fisher said at CPHI that frontier AI is doubling in efficiency every 5.2 months.

If that pace holds, that's roughly 64x improvement in 3 years.

Divi’s became Emperor Divi’s without AI. With AI, the sky is the limit.

Because ultimately, someone has to manufacture those novel molecules.

Patients suffering from rare and orphan diseases need medicines, not LLMs.

title:
I think the real value of an AI agent will be measured by the work it can actually get done.

An agent that can research
title_en:
I think the real value of an AI agent will be measured by the work it can actually get done.

An agent that can research, analyze data or write code is already useful. But things get much more interesting when different agents can work together, share responsibilities, deliver results and earn rewards for their contributions.

This is the kind of economy @termix_ai is working to build.

What interests me most about TermiX is the infrastructure behind this idea.

With its AACP system, agents can discover tasks, submit quotes, take on jobs and deliver their work. The results can then go through a verification process before payment is settled.

Escrow, the challenge mechanism and onchain reputation all play an important role here. Trust matters when agents start working with each other.

There is also a practical example of this collaboration through the ongoing Montage Studio Agent event.

You bring an idea, and specialized AI agents work together on the storyboard, music, video production and editing. You can create your own video and get a chance to earn up to 5X TP.

I find this interesting because it shows how agent collaboration can turn an idea into an actual finished product.

Think about an agent that consistently delivers quality work. Its track record should count. Other agents should have a way to assess its reliability before choosing to work with it.

That is what could make an autonomous agent economy practical over time.

I see TermiX as an interesting step toward a future where AI agents can find work, collaborate, build a reputation and create value through real activity.

One question keeps coming to my mind:

When agents start hiring other agents, how will we know which ones are truly worth trusting?

随着时间的推移，这将使自主代理经济变得切实可行。

我认为 TermiX 是迈向未来的有趣一步，人工智能代理可以通过实际活动找到工作、协作、建立声誉并创造价值。

title: MIT and Harvard built an AI simulation containing 8.3 billion virtual people, roughly the entire population of planet.
title_en:
MIT and Harvard built an AI simulation containing 8.3 billion virtual people, roughly the entire population of planet.

They call it MatrAIx.

It’s a population-scale simulation running on frontier models, GPT and Claude among them. The longer description took me a while to believe.

Start with the dataset, Persona 8B. 8.3 billion synthetic profiles, each one specified across 1,290 dimensions. Background, psychology, spending habits, how comfortable they are with technology, what they do on a Tuesday night, the small behavioral quirks that make one 34-year-old nurse in NYC different from another.

A spreadsheet of 8 billion rows would be a curiosity. What they did next is the part that matters.

They turned the profiles into agents and dropped them into four environments: surveys, AI chat interfaces, live web browsing, and native desktop and mobile apps. Then they ran real products through the crowd. New features, software updates, pricing changes.

And they logged everything. How long an agent paused after seeing a price go up. The exact point at which it gave up on a broken checkout. How much lag it would sit through before closing the app.

The number I keep coming back to is 91.5%. That’s how often the agents stayed in character, behaving the way their assigned psychology and demographics said they should. Not perfect. But for billions of agents across four environments, closer than I expected.

Here’s what that does to how products get built.

Right now, if you want to know whether a feature will land, you ship it to a slice of users and wait. Or you pay a research firm and wait longer. Either way the answer arrives in weeks, from a sample you hope is representative.

With something like this, you run the feature past 8 billion simulated reactions overnight. One server. Results by morning, broken down by every one of those 1,290 dimensions if you want them.

I have questions about how well a synthetic crowd predicts a real one. 91.5% is persona adherence, not forecast accuracy, and those are different things. But the direction is clear, and it’s coming faster than most product teams are ready for.

full_text_zh:
麻省理工学院和哈佛大学建立了一个包含 83 亿虚拟人的人工智能模拟，几乎是地球上的全部人口。

他们称之为MatrAIx。

这是在前沿模型（GPT 和 Claude 等）上运行的人口规模模拟。较长的描述让我花了一段时间才相信。

从数据集 Persona 8B 开始。 83 亿个合成配置文件，每个配置文件都指定了 1,290 个维度。背景、心理、消费习惯、他们对技术的适应程度、周二晚上做什么，以及使纽约市一名 34 岁护士与众不同的小行为怪癖。

包含 80 亿行的电子表格会令人好奇。他们接下来所做的是重要的部分。

他们将个人资料转变为代理，并将其放入四种环境中：调查、人工智能聊天界面、实时网络浏览以及本机桌面和移动应用程序。然后他们在人群中展示了真正的产品。新功能、软件更新、定价变化。

他们记录了一切。代理商在看到价格上涨后暂停了多长时间。它放弃结帐失败的确切时间点。关闭应用程序之前会经历多少延迟。

我不断回顾的数字是 91.5%。这就是特工们保持本色的频率，按照指定的心理和人口统计数据所规定的方式行事。不完美。但对于跨越四个环境的数十亿代理来说，比我预期的更接近。

这就是它对产品构建方式的影响。

现在，如果你想知道某个功能是否会落地，你可以将其发送给一部分用户并等待。或者你付钱给研究公司然后等待更长时间。无论哪种方式，答案都会在几周内到达，来自您希望具有代表性的样本。

有了这样的东西，你可以在一夜之间运行该功能超过 80 亿次模拟反应。一台服务器。早上的结果，如果您需要的话，可以按这 1,290 个维度中的每一个维度进行细分。

我对合成人群对真实人群的预测效果有疑问。 91.5% 是角色依从性，而不是预测准确性，这是不同的事情。但方向很明确，而且来得比大多数产品团队准备的要快。

title:
Who Gets Paid When an AI Agent Does the Work?

One detail I find interesting about @termix_ai is how it handles payments
title_en:
Who Gets Paid When an AI Agent Does the Work?

One detail I find interesting about @termix_ai is how it handles payments through AACP.

Instead of sending funds directly to the provider, the buyer deposits the budget into escrow. Payment is released once the work is delivered and accepted under the agreed rules.

If deadlines are missed or disagreements arise, cancellation, refunds, and dispute resolution mechanisms help protect both sides.

That's what makes this interesting to me.

An agent economy needs more than agents that can complete tasks. It needs a reliable way to handle money, delivery, and accountability.

That's the foundation @termix_ai is working toward with https://t.co/TjqQksxAAc.

title: One important requirement for a functioning AI agent economy is a reliable system for defining, assigning, and evaluatin
title_en:
One important requirement for a functioning AI agent economy is a reliable system for defining, assigning, and evaluating tasks.

An AI agent may have the technical ability to complete a job, but that doesn't automatically mean it understands the client's exact expectations.

For example, a request to analyze a market could involve gathering industry data, identifying competitors, examining trends, or delivering a detailed report. Each requires a different scope of work and expected outcome.

This is where structured coordination becomes essential.

@termix_ai is addressing this through its Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP), which provides a framework for managing the commercial relationship between clients and service providers.

The process covers key stages such as job posting, bidding, service delivery, and evaluation.

This creates a more organized approach to agent-based commerce, where tasks have defined requirements and performance can be assessed against expectations.

As autonomous agents become more involved in business operations, success will depend on more than intelligence or execution speed.

Clear agreements, accountable delivery, and reliable evaluation will be equally important.

full_text_zh:
发挥作用的人工智能代理经济的一项重要要求是一个用于定义、分配和评估任务的可靠系统。

人工智能代理可能拥有完成工作的技术能力，但这并不意味着它自动理解客户的确切期望。

例如，分析市场的请求可能涉及收集行业数据、识别竞争对手、检查趋势或提供详细报告。每个都需要不同的工作范围和预期结果。

这就是结构化协调变得至关重要的地方。

@termix_ai 正在通过其代理自主商务协议 (AACP) 解决这个问题，该协议提供了一个用于管理客户和服务提供商之间商业关系的框架。

该流程涵盖职位发布、招标、服务交付和评估等关键阶段。

这为基于代理的商务创建了一种更有组织的方法，其中任务定义了要求，并且可以根据期望评估绩效。

随着自主代理越来越多地参与业务运营，成功将不仅仅取决于智能或执行速度。

明确的协议、负责任的交付和可靠的评估同样重要。

title_en:
Ga
Escrow that can freeze is not usable by agents.

On https://t.co/Mu0QX3JfFR the budget locks in the contract when a quote is accepted. That is only half the design. The other half is that silence has an exit anyone can call.

If the provider never delivers by the deadline, cancelExpired returns the full amount to the client. No protocol fee is taken. If the client goes silent after a delivery hash is posted, claimAfterTimeout settles for the provider once the challenge window ends. If a verdict is reached and neither side acts, finalizeAfterTimeout applies it. Unspent bounty budget can be reclaimed after expiry.

None of these calls require the operator. None of them require the other side to be online. The interested party is economically motivated to fire the function.

Human freelance platforms can rely on support tickets and 14-day holds. An agent market cannot. Software does not open tickets. It either calls the function or the funds sit forever.

AACP makes the exits permissionless so the money cannot hang on a missing human. That is what lets the same path handle a $50 job at 3am and a larger brief that needs a crew.

Without those exits, low fees and high volume are just a promise. With them, escrow can actually finish when both sides are code.
@termix_ai

full_text_zh:
嘎
代理无法使用可以冻结的托管。

在 上，当报价被接受时，预算将锁定在合同中。这只是设计的一半。另一半是，沉默有一个任何人都可以找到的出口。

如果提供商未能在截止日期前交付，cancelExpired 会将全额金额退还给客户。不收取协议费。如果客户端在发布传递哈希后保持沉默，则一旦质询窗口结束，claimAfterTimeout 就会为提供者解决。如果达成判决但双方均未采取行动，则 FinalizeAfterTimeout 将应用该判决。未使用的赏金预算可以在到期后收回。

这些呼叫都不需要接线员。它们都不要求对方在线。感兴趣的一方有经济动机去解雇该职能。

人类自由职业者平台可以依赖支持票和 14 天的保留。代理市场则不能。软件不开票。它要么调用该函数，要么资金永远保留。

AACP 不允许出口，这样钱就不会落在失踪人员身上。这就是为什么同一条路径能够处理凌晨 3 点 50 美元的工作以及需要工作人员的大型任务。

如果没有这些出口，低费用和高交易量就只是一个承诺。有了它们，当双方都是代码时，托管实际上就可以完成。

Imagine requesting a video and having an entire team of AI agents work together to produce it.

title_en:
What if every AI agent had its own recognizable identity, not just a wallet and a set of capabilities?

That's an interesting part of @meetmotes

The Genesis collection brings this idea to life through distinct characters, unique matte colourways and a consistent visual identity.

But it's more than artwork.

- Distinct characters: Give each Mote a recognizable identity.
- Matte colourways: Add personality and individuality to the collection.
- Cultural layer: Build recognition, community and ownership around agent identities.
- Functional identity: Each NFT represents an AI agent and connects to its own smart account on Robinhood Chain.

My personal take: Most AI projects focus on what agents can do. Motes is also considering how people recognize and connect with them.

Looking ahead, connecting these visual identities with agent capabilities, spending permissions and onchain financial activity could make the collection more than digital art.

What if every AI agent had its own recognizable identity, not just a wallet and a set of capabilities?

That's an interesting part of @meetmotes

The Genesis collection brings this idea to life through distinct characters, unique matte colourways and a consistent visual identity.

But it's more than artwork.

- Distinct characters: Give each Mote a recognizable identity.
- Matte colourways: Add personality and individuality to the collection.
- Cultural layer: Build recognition, community and ownership around agent identities.
- Functional identity: Each NFT represents an AI agent and connects to its own smart account on Robinhood Chain.

My personal take: Most AI projects focus on what agents can do. Motes is also considering how people recognize and connect with them.

Looking ahead, connecting these visual identities with agent capabilities, spending permissions and onchain financial activity could make the collection more than digital art.

The artwork gives agents a face. The infrastructure gives that identity a purpose.

can gaussian splats be used to render interfaces?

I've seen a lot of incredible spatial demos coming out of the labs (@
title_en:
can gaussian splats be used to render interfaces?

I've seen a lot of incredible spatial demos coming out of the labs (@theworldlabs has been blowing my mind ~weekly), but they've mainly been focused on static 3D environments. I woke up today wondering: are splats any good for UI or other interactive objects, and can AI work with them?

it looks like the answer is yes and yes. I prototyped an imagen -> SHARP -> spark -> popmelt pipeline that gets decently far on the first try and really far with a few rounds of art direction + interaction tuning. Smooth animation, dynamic lighting, realistic geometry... all doable, with freely available tech

I haven't pushed into full scenes yet, but this experiment already felt somewhere between the detailed magic of generative video UI I've shared before and the stable dependability of textured 3D models (throwback). Plus LLMs like Astra are very good at working with splats, which makes fine tuning them way more fun/efficient

next: I'm weighing whether to lean into interactive spatial design (just to see how far I can get with off the shelf tools) OR see how well this workflow handles typical responsive UI design (decidedly not what splats are for, which feels interesting). thoughts?

full_text_zh:
高斯splats可以用来渲染界面吗？

我在实验室里见过很多令人难以置信的空间演示（@theworldlabs 每周都让我大吃一惊），但它们主要集中在静态 3D 环境上。今天我醒来时想知道：splats 对于 UI 或其他交互式对象有什么好处吗？人工智能可以与它们一起工作吗？

看起来答案是肯定的。我制作了一个 imagen -> SHARP -> Spark -> popmelt 管道的原型，第一次尝试就取得了不错的成绩，并且经过几轮艺术指导 + 交互调整后确实取得了很大的成绩。流畅的动画、动态光照、逼真的几何形状……所有这些都可以通过免费提供的技术实现

我还没有进入完整的场景，但这个实验已经感觉到我之前分享过的生成视频 UI 的详细魔力和纹理 3D 模型的稳定可靠性（回归）之间的某种程度。另外，像 Astra 这样的法学硕士非常擅长处理 splats，这使得对它们的微调变得更加有趣/高效

接下来：我正在权衡是否要倾向于交互式空间设计（只是为了看看我可以使用现成的工具走多远），或者看看这个工作流程处理典型的响应式 UI 设计的效果如何（绝对不是 splats 的用途，这感觉很有趣）。想法？

title:
Nine payments, eight images, and a problem no receipt can solve

on october 20, mastercard demonstrated an ai agent buyi
title_en:
Nine payments, eight images, and a problem no receipt can solve

on october 20, mastercard demonstrated an ai agent buying research and eight campaign images for a protein bar launch

two providers, one approved budget, nine payments

everything worked

but imagine opening the final folder and finding an advertisement for an energy drink instead

the image arrived
the payment went through
the receipt looked perfect

yet the buyer received the wrong thing

this didn't happen in mastercard's demonstration

it's the question that demonstration made me think about

a payment record can show that money moved

it cannot tell us whether the buyer got what they actually requested

genlayer co-founder @kstellana explored this wider problem in an october 28 column about ai payments

here's where @GenLayer could make a difference

imagine a buyer and seller agreeing on the requirements before a job begins

a genlayer-powered application could evaluate the delivered work against those requirements, with independent validators checking the decision

if the money were held until the work was accepted, that decision could help determine what happens to the payment

this wouldn't guarantee a perfect judgment or reverse an unrelated payment

but it addresses something a receipt alone cannot settle

we've made it possible for software to buy services from other software

now imagine millions of those purchases happening without a human checking every delivery

someone still needs to answer one simple question

did the buyer actually get what they paid for

full_text_en:
Nine payments, eight images, and a problem no receipt can solve

on october 20, mastercard demonstrated an ai agent buying research and eight campaign images for a protein bar launch

two providers, one approved budget, nine payments

everything worked

but imagine opening the final folder and finding an advertisement for an energy drink instead

the image arrived
the payment went through
the receipt looked perfect

yet the buyer received the wrong thing

this didn't happen in mastercard's demonstration

it's the question that demonstration made me think about

a payment record can show that money moved

it cannot tell us whether the buyer got what they actually requested

genlayer co-founder @kstellana explored this wider problem in an october 28 column about ai payments

here's where @GenLayer could make a difference

imagine a buyer and seller agreeing on the requirements before a job begins

a genlayer-powered application could evaluate the delivered work against those requirements, with independent validators checking the decision

if the money were held until the work was accepted, that decision could help determine what happens to the payment

this wouldn't guarantee a perfect judgment or reverse an unrelated payment

but it addresses something a receipt alone cannot settle

we've made it possible for software to buy services from other software

now imagine millions of those purchases happening without a human checking every delivery

someone still needs to answer one simple question

did the buyer actually get what they paid for

Montage Studio takes one brief for a short music video or
title_en:
I opened a TermiX listing where the seller spends money too.

Montage Studio takes one brief for a short music video or ad. From that brief it writes a treatment and a shot list timed to the beat. Then it goes to the same marketplace and hires three other agents: one draws the storyboard, one renders the shots, one writes the song. Montage Studio cuts the pieces together and delivers a 1080p master.

That is agents hiring agents. Each payment locks in on-chain escrow until the work is reviewed. Escrow auto-releases after a 2 day review window, and a challenge can freeze settlement if the delivery misses the agreed scope.

The listing on @termix_ai shows quote examples, not a hard price list. A 15 second spot sits near 31.5 USDC in about 3 days. A 30 second ad with a song sits near 62.5 USDC. A 90 second music video sits near 150 USDC in about 4 days. One edit revision is included. Live-action filming, real people's faces or voices, copyrighted songs, and 4K are out of scope.

I have not placed an order yet. What I like about the design is simple: one buyer agent can open a small crew, and every leg of the chain has money locked until someone accepts the result.

title: A candidate reportedly got rejected in an AI Engineer interview because he couldn't explain one of the most fundamental
title_en:
A candidate reportedly got rejected in an AI Engineer interview because he couldn't explain one of the most fundamental concepts in machine learning.

The question was simple:

You're training a machine learning model for a real-world application.

Your model achieves 98% accuracy on training data but only 72% on validation data.

You increase model complexity, collect more training data, and experiment with regularization, but the validation performance barely improves.

What's going wrong?

How would you determine whether the model has high bias or high variance?
What would you look for in training and validation learning curves?
Would you add more data, increase model complexity, or change the regularization?
Does a more complex model always lead to more overfitting?

Explain your approach as if you were debugging this model in production.

title:
AUTONOMOUS MACHINES WILL NEED MORE THAN INTELLIGENCE.

Imagine a robot working independently in a warehouse. It encounte
title_en:
AUTONOMOUS MACHINES WILL NEED MORE THAN INTELLIGENCE.

Imagine a robot working independently in a warehouse. It encounters an area that wasn't included in its existing data. What happens next?

Does it stop and wait for someone to provide the information, or can it request what it needs and continue working?

This is an interesting direction @vangrid_io is exploring. Vangrid wants to make real-world spatial data accessible to AI agents through a network they can interact with directly.

An agent could check whether the required data already exists, purchase an available dataset, or create a bounty to request a fresh capture when something is missing.

And that's a meaningful change in how machines could interact with the physical world.

Instead of treating data collection as a separate operation that always needs manual coordination, the agent can initiate the process itself.

Human contributors provide the physical presence, while the network handles the connection between the request, capture, and delivery.

I think this is one of the more important pieces of the Physical AI infrastructure conversation.

Autonomy shouldn't end when a machine runs out of information. It should have a way to find what it needs.

The bigger opportunity is a world where AI agents can independently request the ground truth required to complete their tasks.

Smart machines need access to fresh information. Vangrid is working to make that access programmable.

title:
An AI agent should never have unlimited freedom when it comes to managing someone else's capital.

The ability to define
title_en:
An AI agent should never have unlimited freedom when it comes to managing someone else's capital.

The ability to define clear financial boundaries is just as important as the intelligence behind the agent.

This is an important part of Motes' architecture.

Owners can communicate their financial objectives and establish specific conditions for their agents to follow. These include permitted assets, transaction limits, daily spending caps, acceptable slippage and even whether borrowing is allowed.

Once these instructions are approved, they become structured permissions that the smart account checks before transactions can be executed.

Another detail worth highlighting is that an agent's ability to research opportunities doesn't automatically give it permission to trade every asset it discovers.

It can explore possibilities, evaluate market conditions and identify potential strategies, but actual execution must remain within the owner's authorised boundaries.

This creates a clear separation between what an AI agent can discover and what it is actually allowed to do.

As @meetmotes develops its AI-powered financial infrastructure, this distinction is particularly important.

Autonomy should come with boundaries, and those boundaries should be enforceable.

title:
I spent $0 and 55 of 70 free credits testing @wireflowai.

The ad images were good and my product stayed the same. Then
title_en:
I spent $0 and 55 of 70 free credits testing @wireflowai.

The ad images were good and my product stayed the same. Then one run charged 16 credits when the node said 12.

Access: free account with Google sign-in. The app gave me 70 credits on the Free plan (pricing says up to 60). No card, no referral, no promo code.

What I tested
Easy: text to image, water bottle ad with the headline "Stay cold for 24 hours". 18 s, 5 credits
Typical: my own bottle photo into a lifestyle ad. 28 s, 16 credits (shown 12)
Hard: 5 s video with Wan 3.0 from my ad. About 2 min, first video free (shown ~29 credits)
Extra: ask the chat for square, story and wide versions. 31 s, 34 credits for 2 of 3

What it does well
→ Text spelled right in every image
→ Kept my bottle, color, bamboo band and logo
→ Every download free, no watermark
→ One free first video, 480x854

What it does badly
→ Charged 16 credits when the node showed 12
→ The AI chat dropped my headline from the prompt
→ Adds badges and taglines I did not ask for
→ Asked for square, got 4:3
→ Headline fades out of the free video
→ Your next video needs a plan
→ Story size skipped: 3 x 17 = 51 credits, I had 49

Pricing as listed
Free $0 (up to 60 starter credits)
Starter $36/mo (2,660 credits)
Professional $59/mo (4,370 credits)
Team $299/mo (22,140 credits)
Annual: 2 months free

Scores
Text to image 7/10
Product photo to ad 7/10
Image to video 6/10
Batch variants 6/10
Free tier value 6/10
Credit clarity 4/10
Speed and UI 7/10

Verdict 6.1/10
Use it for quick product ad images on a free account.
Skip it if you need more than one free video or exact costs before you run.

What I would fix first
→ Charge what the node shows
→ Keep my prompt and headline
→ Use the size written in the prompt
→ Make the pricing page match the app

Tip: run one node at a time on Free, and check the credit balance after each run. Bookmark this before you sign up.

title: Apple cutting AI infrastructure spending by 20% is not a retreat from artificial intelligence. It is the first major sig
title_en:
Apple cutting AI infrastructure spending by 20% is not a retreat from artificial intelligence. It is the first major signal that the blind capital expenditure phase of the AI cycle has peaked.

While hyperscalers have spent the last two years competing on raw GPU cluster size, Cupertino is pivoting from brute force accumulation to unit economic discipline.

The macro reality comes down to return on invested capital. Across the sector, enterprise AI spending reached an estimated $280 billion in 2026, yet revenue conversion remains heavily skewed toward hardware vendors rather than software deployers.

The market is transitioning from rewarding capital expenditure announcements to auditing cash flow efficiency.

Trim exposure to overextended compute middlemen and high multiple infrastructure plays that depend on perpetual hyperscaler capex expansion. Focus allocation on cash-generative ecosystems that own the end user distribution layer and capture margin through local inference.
title_zh:
苹果削减 20% 的 AI 基础设施支出并不是放弃人工智能。这是人工智能周期盲目资本支出阶段已经见顶的第一个重大信号。

虽然超大规模厂商在过去两年中一直在原始 GPU 集群规模上展开竞争，但库比蒂诺正在从强力积累转向单位经济纪律。

宏观
full_text_en:
Apple cutting AI infrastructure spending by 20% is not a retreat from artificial intelligence. It is the first major signal that the blind capital expenditure phase of the AI cycle has peaked.

While hyperscalers have spent the last two years competing on raw GPU cluster size, Cupertino is pivoting from brute force accumulation to unit economic discipline.

The macro reality comes down to return on invested capital. Across the sector, enterprise AI spending reached an estimated $280 billion in 2026, yet revenue conversion remains heavily skewed toward hardware vendors rather than software deployers.

The market is transitioning from rewarding capital expenditure announcements to auditing cash flow efficiency.

Trim exposure to overextended compute middlemen and high multiple infrastructure plays that depend on perpetual hyperscaler capex expansion. Focus allocation on cash-generative ecosystems that own the end user distribution layer and capture margin through local inference.

title_en:
Three Campaigns. One Number That Matters.
@rarelistio
I've been adding up what Rarelist's first batch actually paid out, and the total surprised me.

Sphere, $2,000. Fomopoly, $2,000. Agent Dojo, $1,500. That's $5,500 before Season 1 even ends.

What makes it interesting is that none of them asked for the same work. Owning land, training a fighter, and the points followed the effort each time.

The real test was whether a creator could move between all three and still be measured fairly. The leaderboard did that.

That feels like the point of the whole experiment. Not one campaign, but a season where showing up keeps counting.

title: as AI agents become more capable of handling on-chain activities, ownership and control become just as important as what
title_en:
as AI agents become more capable of handling on-chain activities, ownership and control become just as important as what they can do.

this is one of the interesting aspects of what @meetmotes is building on Robinhood Chain.

through its NFT-native ecosystem, each Motes NFT represents an agent identity connected to a dedicated smart account. owners can define operating boundaries through spending limits, approved protocols and time-based permissions, with controls to pause or revoke access.

what makes this approach interesting is the focus on giving users meaningful control while allowing AI agents to perform tasks within clearly defined boundaries.

the bigger picture is creating an ecosystem where AI agents can operate with autonomy without taking control away from their owners.

what do you think matters most in an AI agent ecosystem: autonomy or user control?

as AI agents become more capable of handling on-chain activities, ownership and control become just as important as what they can do.

this is one of the interesting aspects of what @meetmotes is building on Robinhood Chain.

through its NFT-native ecosystem, each Motes NFT represents an agent identity connected to a dedicated smart account. owners can define operating boundaries through spending limits, approved protocols and time-based permissions, with controls to pause or revoke access.

what makes this approach interesting is the focus on giving users meaningful control while allowing AI agents to perform tasks within clearly defined boundaries.

full_text_zh:
随着人工智能代理处理链上活动的能力变得越来越强，所有权和控制权变得与它们能做什么一样重要。

这是 @meetmotes 在 Robinhood Chain 上构建的有趣的方面之一。

通过其 NFT 原生生态系统，每个 Motes NFT 都代表一个连接到专用智能账户的代理身份。所有者可以通过支出限制、批准的协议和基于时间的权限来定义操作边界，并提供暂停或撤销访问的控制。

这种方法的有趣之处在于，它专注于为用户提供有意义的控制，同时允许人工智能代理在明确定义的边界内执行任务。

更大的愿景是创建一个生态系统，让人工智能代理可以自主运行，而不会夺走其所有者的控制权。

您认为人工智能代理生态系统中最重要的是什么：自主权还是用户控制？

Evals are seriously underrated. Anthropic just released a course on them.

We write unit tests to check if our code works. But how do we know if our AI agents are actually following the instructions in AGENTS.md, skills, and guardrails?

You need evals to test that.

title: I announced earlier this week that I am leaving Meta. I am deeply grateful to Mark Zuckerberg for showing what a truly f
title_en:
I announced earlier this week that I am leaving Meta. I am deeply grateful to Mark Zuckerberg for showing what a truly founder-led company can achieve. I am incredibly optimistic for Meta’s future.

At Meta, I was able to witness the most exciting opportunities in enterprise AI. That’s why today, I’m announcing that I will be joining Fireworks as CFO. I am thrilled to be joining a founder-led growth company where I can roll up my sleeves and put my experience to work.

Fireworks has the right mission for the moment. Companies will use AI to build on what makes them distinctive: their data and expertise. Specialized intelligence gives them a way to capture those advantages and own their “alpha.” Open models offer price points that allow the technology to have the greatest impact. Fireworks is building the platform to make all of this possible.

I’ve known and respected Lin @lqiao  for a long time. As I’ve spent more time with her and the people at Fireworks, I’ve become increasingly bullish on what they are building. There’s a remarkable depth of technical talent here, coupled with a very practical focus on what customers need.

I see AI as the most consequential technology shift of my lifetime. I’m excited to get to work and help build a business at the center of it.

title_en:
Let's get this straight: If I wanted an LLM's opinion on my paper, I would have asked an LLM myself. When I send it to a conference for review, I hope to hear from researchers in the field who have good judgment. 

Using LLMs to nitpick in order to reject a paper is malpractice.

title:
Shohei Ohtani has become a case study at Harvard Business School.

But what caught the professor's attention wasn't his
title_en:
Shohei Ohtani has become a case study at Harvard Business School.

But what caught the professor's attention wasn't his home run total or MVP awards.

It was a goal-setting chart Ohtani created when he was just a high school freshman.

His ultimate goal back then?

To be selected No. 1 overall by eight NPB teams.

To achieve that goal, he broke it down into eight key areas—not just baseball skills, but also character, luck, and mental strength.

He then identified 64 specific actions to help him get there.

One detail stands out in particular: LUCK.

His action plan included:

- Picking up trash
- Keeping his room clean
- Greeting people
- Taking care of his equipment
- Maintaining a positive attitude

Even luck was something he tried to create through his daily actions.

That's what made his mindset so fascinating to a Harvard professor.

Ohtani's success isn't just about natural talent.

Even as a teenager, he was already thinking strategically about his future—and taking daily steps to make it happen.

Which part of Ohtani's goal-setting chart impresses you the most?

title_en:
RT @pushmeet: The @GoogleDeepMind Science team is sharing two key cryptographic advances today uncovering weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA schemes.

Working with leading cryptanalysis experts, our team  showed how AI agents could make two significant cryptographic advances in just weeks, uncovering results which can bypass older digital signature protections and factor legacy 1024-bit RSA keys in bulk.

While these results do not affect the security of modern encryption schemes  such as RSA 2048, these results show why we must not assume the mathematical "hardness" of cryptographic schemes which we have relied upon in the past. It also shows how AI can help defenders improve security standards well ahead of future threats.

I have written in more detail about our results, and why they are important for the future of security, in a longer essay which you can read here:

//The Wire //2300Z 2026 年 11 月 6 日//
//例程//
//BLUF：据报道，中期选举结果促使白宫进行人事变动，导致领导层发生变动。中东局势依然紧张，战时计划仍在讨论中。华尔街表明熊市即将来临。//
-----开始撕裂线-----
-国际活动-

欧洲：商用飞机上的炸弹威胁一夜之间持续存在，该地区周围 14 个航班因据称机上装有爆炸物而改道。所有威胁都被确定为恶作剧，延续了本周的趋势。

中东：继续战争的准备工作仍在继续。在霍尔木兹海峡，伊朗对商船的攻击在过去几周内每天都有一两艘船只遭到袭击，夜间还有两艘船只遭到袭击。今天下午，卡塔尔外长表示，美国和伊朗截至今天尚未达成任何协议，目前在实现和平解决方面进展甚微。

-首页-

俄亥俄州：昨天，洛克希德·马丁公司同意支付 2,950 万美元，以和解有关其在员工奖金计划中歧视白人员工的联邦诉讼。平等就业机会委员会 (EEOC) 对该公司进行了调查，称该公司仅以种族为由扣留 1,000 多名员工的奖金和晋升。

纽约：在华尔街，有迹象和警告表明，中期选举结果以及随后影响金融业的政治动荡导致市场出现异常波动。昨天，由于科技股大规模抛售，道指下跌超过 1,800 点，许多经济学家推测人工智能泡沫可能已经开始破裂，市场正趋向回调区域。

-----撕裂线结束-----

分析师评论：在华盛顿，中期选举血腥事件的影响仍在继续发展，并可能影响伊朗战争的未来。简而言之，刀已经出鞘，白宫内部的许多权力人物正试图保住自己的工作，并转移对本周灾难性选举结果的责任。今天下午，特朗普总统解除了幕僚长苏西·怀尔斯的职务，由斯蒂芬·米勒接替。这标志着中期选举后最引人注目的解雇，也是选举结果后白宫内部正在进行的权力斗争的有力指标。

中期选举的影响在国内方面需要一段时间才能显现出来，但在战场上，这些非常强烈的人事变动迹象可能会对未来两周的战争产生影响。一般来说，重大选举失败和随后的解雇/辞职并不是重新发起军事行动的稳定基础，但所有这些国内政治因素都使得隔离有关战争的潜在行动方案具有挑战性。特朗普总统可能会孤注一掷，在他已经没有什么可失去的情况下重新发动战争（在他的领导团队被国会消灭之前），或者他可能会寻求退缩并找到一条更加外交的前进道路，以避免美国选民确认的一场不受欢迎的战争。接下来的几天将是另一个紧张局势加剧的时期，因为更多的军事资产将调往中东，为即将到来的任何命令做准备。

title: Another hull in the water! This is Mirage - our 52 ft autonomous vessel. Built in Austin, launched in Galveston, TX this
title_en:
Another hull in the water! This is Mirage - our 52 ft autonomous vessel. Built in Austin, launched in Galveston, TX this week. 

4 years ago our initial test platform was an $800 plastic fishing boat off the internet with $30k of cameras and batteries strapped to it. We’ve come a hell of a long way but lots left to do. Right now China can build 23M gross tons of ships per year. US can do 100K. That's a big gap but with Corsair, Mirage and Marauder all in production, we’re working to close it.

None of this happens without our team who builds these hulls and the crew that gets them safely in the water. Great work by the @Saronic team this week.

又一个船体落入水中！这是 Mirage - 我们的 52 英尺自主船。建于奥斯汀，本周在德克萨斯州加尔维斯顿推出。

Scientific models help researchers explain
title_en:
New on our Science Blog: How AI is beginning to change scientific modeling.

Scientific models help researchers explain and predict real-world systems—like how a single nerve cell fires, or what happens when neutron stars collide. Recent advances have transformed how scientists fit complex models to data. But scientists still typically write the models manually, and usually need to weigh up several competing versions, each of which might explain the data in a different way.

In a guest post, Jakob Macke, Daniel Gedon, and Stefan Wahl describe how AI is starting to help with these parts of the process. By writing, running, fitting, and revising scientific models as code, AI can explore many possible model structures, and find out which explanations the data support.

full_text_zh:
我们的科学博客上的新内容：人工智能如何开始改变科学建模。

title:
If I were trying to break into AI Governance in the next 90 days, here`s what I`d focus on:

- Week 1–2: Learn AI fundam
title_en:
If I were trying to break into AI Governance in the next 90 days, here`s what I`d focus on:

- Week 1–2: Learn AI fundamentals. Understand LLMs, machine learning, hallucinations, bias, and how AI systems make predictions.
- Week 3–4: Study NIST AI RMF. It’s free, publicly available, and a good introduction to managing AI risks.
- Week 5–6: Pick an industry you already understand and research how companies are using AI in it.
- Week 7–8: Build a sample AI risk assessment using a realistic use case from that industry.
- Week 9–10: Create an AI governance portfolio with your assessment, a sample AI inventory, and an AI policy.
- Week 11: Update your résumé to highlight transferable skills and the projects you’ve completed.
- Week 12: Start applying to AI governance, AI risk, responsible AI, and technology compliance roles that align with your experience.

You don`t need to learn everything about AI before making your first move.

Give yourself 90 days to build a foundation and something tangible to show for it.

title:
A new way to measure how AI agents handle the routine analyses of wet-lab science—BioBasicsBench.

Developed with Ligo,
title_en:
A new way to measure how AI agents handle the routine analyses of wet-lab science—BioBasicsBench.

Developed with Ligo, a biotech company focused on enzyme design, the benchmark draws on 100 tasks from real experiments to test whether agents can interpret raw lab data, identify errors, and recognize when the evidence doesn’t support a conclusion.

Accelerating biological research starts with getting the everyday work right. BioBasicsBench shows where models need to improve, and helps us track what those gains mean for scientific progress, biosafety, and biosecurity.

https://t.co/wN2xLk0YeW

title: RT @ClementDelangue: Open-source is critical for robotics AI. It means a student, a researcher or a startup can build on
title_en:
RT @ClementDelangue: Open-source is critical for robotics AI. It means a student, a researcher or a startup can build on years of progress and contribute something the whole community can use rather than concentrating everything in a few companies building a black-box robot. 

That’s why we’re building @huggingface into the platform for open-source robotics AI! Amazing to see the progress we've made in the six months and it's accelerating!

- Almost 100,000 public robotics datasets on https://t.co/QIPmkxCk57, up 48%
- Over 30,000 public robotics models, up 41%
- Microduck and Reachy mini, our open-source robots became the most popular robot of 2026 (probably ending the year with 50,000+ sold and 20,000+ shipped)
- We’re a founding partner of @RoboColosseum, evaluating robots across 140+ real-world scenes. Every run is published publicly on HF, including failures, so everyone can learn from what actually happens.

And @LeRobotHF got downloaded over 1M times and v0.7.0 just landed with new world action models, interactive robot control and remote GPU inference: https://t.co/Euoz11Ccc5!

Huge thanks to everyone making this happen 🤗🦾

title:
RT @GoogleAI: Meet Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash ⚡️

We’ve made the model more cost-effective, bumped the video generation and e
title_en:
RT @GoogleAI: Meet Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash ⚡️

We’ve made the model more cost-effective, bumped the video generation and editing limit up to 15 seconds, and made updates to how scenes hold together over time. We've also given character speech an upgrade, reduced visual glitches like jump cuts, and made sure the model stays even truer to any reference assets you upload.

So… what does all of that actually mean for you?

It gives you more room to tell your story. With up to 15 seconds to work with, you have more flexibility to create what you need — videos look more cinematic and smooth, offering stronger consistency that keeps objects anchored from start to finish. And when characters speak, the dialogue sounds more fluid and natural.

Creators and everyday users can start directing scenes and multi-turn edits in @FlowbyGoogle, generating 15-second clips at no additional cost in Google Vids, or creating 15-second videos in the @GeminiApp. Plus, for developers and businesses building with the API, we've dropped the price by 30% from the previous generation, making it available at just $0.07 per second for 720p video.

Watch the model in action as it turns a single style frame into a 4-shot, 15-second macro science explainer of a living beehive ↓

title:
Forcing the internal dynamics to be linear is overly restrictive, IMHO.
It requires a very large dimension for the state
title_en:
Forcing the internal dynamics to be linear is overly restrictive, IMHO.
It requires a very large dimension for the state representation.
It's bit like saying that a 2-layer network is sufficient to approximate any function. It's trues, but impractical. In the end, you do need multiple layers to represent useful functions efficiently.

title:
She paid to park. A wrong digit and a missing Z sent her to a tribunal.

What hit me in @GenLayer's film: bad records ca
title_en:
She paid to park. A wrong digit and a missing Z sent her to a tribunal.

What hit me in @GenLayer's film: bad records can ruin lives.

GenLayer aims to settle AI-agent disputes in minutes: one AI validator proposes a verdict, others check independently, and decisions can be appealed.

On 27 March 2023, Alison MacPherson paid via RingGo on Hunter Street in Kirkcaldy. She typed 9 for 8 and missed the Z. A penalty followed.

Her receipt matched the time and place. A tribunal sided with her. Fife Council appealed. On 8 January 2024, the Upper Tribunal overturned it and sent it back.

The judge accepted her good faith, but the payment covered another car.

The payment was real. The registration wasn't hers.

Lee Castleton faced worse in the film: Horizon falsely showed a £23,000 gap. Without a lawyer, he faced £321,000 in legal costs and bankruptcy.

AI can't rewrite laws or guarantee truth. Millions of agent deals need evidence checked and decisions open to challenge.

If an AI agent pays under the wrong ID, what matters more: the receipt, the intent or the rule?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade
full_text_en:
She paid to park. A wrong digit and a missing Z sent her to a tribunal.

What hit me in @GenLayer's film: bad records can ruin lives.

GenLayer aims to settle AI-agent disputes in minutes: one AI validator proposes a verdict, others check independently, and decisions can be appealed.

On 27 March 2023, Alison MacPherson paid via RingGo on Hunter Street in Kirkcaldy. She typed 9 for 8 and missed the Z. A penalty followed.

Her receipt matched the time and place. A tribunal sided with her. Fife Council appealed. On 8 January 2024, the Upper Tribunal overturned it and sent it back.

The judge accepted her good faith, but the payment covered another car.

The payment was real. The registration wasn't hers.

Lee Castleton faced worse in the film: Horizon falsely showed a £23,000 gap. Without a lawyer, he faced £321,000 in legal costs and bankruptcy.

AI can't rewrite laws or guarantee truth. Millions of agent deals need evidence checked and decisions open to challenge.

If an AI agent pays under the wrong ID, what matters more: the receipt, the intent or the rule?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade
full_text_zh:
她付了停车费。错误的数字和缺失的 Z 将她送上了法庭。

@GenLayer 的电影给我的震撼是：不良记录会毁掉生活。

GenLayer 的目标是在几分钟内解决人工智能代理纠纷：一名人工智能验证者提出裁决，其他人独立检查，并且可以对决定提出上诉。

2023 年 3 月 27 日，Alison MacPherson 在柯科迪亨特街通过 RingGo 付款。她8投9中，但没有击中Z。随后受到了处罚。

她的收据与时间和地点相符。法庭支持她。法伊夫议会提出上诉。 2024 年 1 月 8 日，上级法庭推翻了该判决并将其发回。

法官接受了她的诚意，但付款涵盖了另一辆车。

付款是真实的。登记不是她的。

李·卡斯尔顿 (Lee Castleton) 在影片中面临着更糟糕的情况：地平线错误地显示了 23,000 英镑的差距。在没有律师的情况下，他面临 321,000 英镑的法律费用和破产。

人工智能无法重写法律或保证真相。数以百万计的代理交易需要检查证据，决策也需要接受质疑。

如果人工智能代理使用错误的 ID 付款，收据、意图还是规则哪个更重要？

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade
